closure.closure_target: Default-deny raw HTML and sanitize rendered output; ensure templates escape all user-controlled fields; add security regression tests with representative payloads.

closure.closure_target: Define supported encodings and filename rules; normalize paths consistently at ingestion and link-resolution; add cross-platform fixtures and CI matrix.

closure.closure_target: Guarantee unique canonical IDs (path-based) and emit hard warnings/errors on collisions; provide collision resolution policy (e.g., include directory segments or hash suffix).

closure.closure_target: Implement basePath/baseUrl consistently across: page links, backlinks, tag links, search index URL, and static assets; add a deployment test matrix.

critical_findings.finding: The monolithic, in-memory architecture (O1) is likely to crash or hang with excessive memory usage when processing a legitimate but large-scale note collection (e.g., several thousand notes, or notes with very large text bodies), making the tool unusable for users who exceed the undocumented or un-enforced scale limits.

A user inadvertently publishes a static site containing sensitive or private notes to a public web host. Because access control is a non-goal, the tool facilitates this high-impact data leakage. The planned 'documentation-only' mitigation is insufficient for a critical risk.

A user pastes content from an untrusted source containing malicious JavaScript into a note. Without mandatory server-side sanitization, the script is rendered into the final HTML and executes in the browser of anyone viewing the note, leading to a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability.

A user's notes, which use a common but non-default convention like `[[WikiLinks]]`, are processed successfully but result in a site with broken navigation because the required link parsing convention was not explicitly configured. This silently breaks a core feature of the system (backlinks/linking).

The generated client-side search index for a moderately large note collection becomes excessively large, causing long page load times and unresponsive search UI in the browser. This makes a primary feature unusable and degrades the overall site experience.

The system generates the same output path for two different source notes (e.g., 'notes/topicA.md' and 'archive/topicA.md') due to a naive slug generation strategy. This causes one note to be silently overwritten in the output, resulting in data loss and broken backlink references.

The build process is non-deterministic, generating different output for the same input on subsequent runs (e.g., due to unstable sort order of tags/files or embedded timestamps). This creates excessive noise in version control, undermining a key workflow for managing static sites.
